title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is page 2 of a 1981-82 set of notes on stratified spaces and conic neighbourhoods. Page 1 sketched the 'unfolded' picture: unfolded strata Σ_i, connecting tubes Σ_ij, junctions Σ_ijk, indexed by flags in a poset I. This page lays the point-set foundation. It answers the question: what exactly is 'a stratification of X indexed by a poset I'?

(1) Specialization preorder. A space X gives a preorder Ord(X) by x ≤ y iff cl{x} ⊂ cl{y}. This preorder is an order iff X is T0.

(2) Alexandrov topology. A preordered set I gives a space Esp(I):
- closed sets are the down-sets;
- open sets are the up-sets, i.e. the closed sets of I°;
- a basis of opens is given by the I_{≥x};
- cl{x} = I_{≤x}, so x ≤ y iff x ∈ cl{y}.

(3) Basic facts.
- NB1: a map between preorders is monotone iff it is continuous.
- NB2: a topology comes from a (necessarily unique) preorder iff arbitrary unions of closed sets are closed, i.e. iff an 'opposite topology' exists. These are the Alexandrov spaces.
- Ord∘Esp = id on preorders, and there is a natural continuous identity Esp(Ord X) → X. It is a homeomorphism iff X is Alexandrov.
- Hence Esp ⊣ Ord: Hom_Top(Esp I, X) ≅ Hom_Preord(I, Ord X). In particular a map I → X is continuous iff it is monotone.

(4) Stratifications as maps to posets. A map φ: X → I is the same as a pseudo-partition X = ⊔ X_i^* (empty pieces allowed). Write X_J^* = φ^{-1}(J).
- φ is continuous iff each X^*_{≥i} is open, iff each X^*_{≱i} is closed.
- Necessary condition: the X_i := X^*_{≤i} are closed.
- This is sufficient if I is finite, or if φ is locally finite (each point has a neighbourhood meeting finitely many pieces).
- Remark: the Alexandrov topology of a sub-preorder is the induced topology.

(5) Inverse problem. When is the (pre)order on I determined by the partition, and when does an order making φ continuous exist and is it unique?
- Uniqueness needs φ surjective (or card I ≤ 1 if X is empty).
- Ideal situation: I carries the quotient topology, i.e. X_J closed iff J closed.
- For φ locally finite, the quotient topology on I is Alexandrov, so it comes from a unique preorder: i ≤ j iff every J with X_J^* closed and j ∈ J contains i.
- This preorder is an order (quotient T0) iff cl(X_i^*) ∩ (open saturation of X_i^*) = X_i^*. Here the closure is the smallest saturated closed set and the open saturation is the smallest saturated open set containing X_i^*.

(6) Definition. Grothendieck proposes to call 'stratification fidèle' a locally finite equivalence relation whose quotient preorder is an order. Equivalently, it is a family (X_i^*) indexed by an ordered set with:
- (a) the X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j^* are closed, which forces the X_i^* to be locally closed;
- (b) X_J closed ⇒ J closed.

The next page refines this. φ open corresponds to the frontier condition cl(X_j^*) = ∪_{i≤j} X_i^*. 'Stratification stricte' is then characterized by increasing closed families with X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k plus density conditions. In modern terms, a stratification is a continuous map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology, plus fidelity and frontier conditions.
errors: The identities as written on the page appear to have swapped subscripts. With ℰ = (Esp) and 𝒪 = (Préord), Ord∘Esp is an endofunctor of 𝒪 and should equal id_𝒪, while Esp∘Ord → id_ℰ. This is a notational slip, either in the manuscript or in the transcription; the accompanying justification via id_X continuous from Esp Ord X to X is correct.

The sufficiency of 'X_i closed' for continuity needs local finiteness in the sense that each point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many X_j^*. With that reading the argument (a locally finite union of closed sets is closed) is correct; the page's wording of 'loc. finie' is cut off.
The fidelity criterion is stated somewhat tentatively, with crossed-out attempts. Read as 'the Alexandrov quotient is T0 iff cl(i) ∩ (smallest open containing i) = {i}', it is correct.

ideas.what: Specialization preorder of a space; order iff T0
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Alexandrov 1937; standard in EGA for schemes)

ideas.what: Topology on a preordered set with down-sets closed; arbitrary unions of closed sets closed characterizes such spaces
Adjunction Esp ⊣ Ord between preorders and topological spaces, with Ord∘Esp = id
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov-space / specialization adjunction (coreflection of Top onto Alexandrov spaces)

ideas.what: A stratification of X indexed by a poset I is a continuous map φ: X → I with I given the Alexandrov topology; continuity iff the X_{≤i} are closed (locally finite case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie, Higher Algebra Appendix A.5 (c. 2009-2017); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; Barwick–Glasman–Haine 'Exodromy' (2018); Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratifications but, to my knowledge, not this formalism

ideas.what: Recovering the poset of strata as the quotient topology on I (Alexandrov for locally finite partitions); fidelity = quotient is T0, i.e. cl(X_i^*) ∩ open-saturation(X_i^*) = X_i^*
ideas.modern_name: poset of strata as T0 quotient / 'conservative' stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in modern stratified homotopy theory (Haine, Douteau, Waas); no single standard attribution

missed.claim: In 1981-82 Grothendieck explicitly defines stratifications as (locally finite) continuous maps X → I to a poset with the Alexandrov topology. He derives the continuity criterion (the X_{≤i} closed) via the Esp ⊣ Ord adjunction. This is exactly the definition that became standard in higher-categorical stratified homotopy theory around 2009-2018 (Lurie HA A.5, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Barwick–Glasman–Haine), where it is not attributed to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Considérons maintenant φ : X → I, i.e. une pseudo-partition X = ∪ X_i^* ... Continue ssi φ^{-1}(I_{≥i}) ouverts
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point for the foundational definition used in exodromy and stratified homotopy hypotheses. It shows Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme starting from the same formalism.

missed.claim: Grothendieck links fidelity of a stratification (the poset of strata recovered intrinsically) to T0-ness of the Alexandrov quotient topology on I. On the next page he links the frontier condition to openness of φ. These give a purely topological dictionary between conditions on stratifications and properties of the map to the Alexandrov space. Modern treatments (Douteau, Waas, Haine) discuss refinement and coarsening of stratifications but rarely state this dictionary in this form.
missed.quote: On pourrait appeler "stratification fidèle" de X une relation d'équiv. loc. finie telle que l'ens préordonné quotient X soit ordonné
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This offers clean intrinsic criteria for when the stratifying poset is determined by the decomposition. That is relevant to defining canonical (coarsest or minimal) stratifications in tame/o-minimal settings, which the next page explicitly raises.

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks how to state that the topology of I is the quotient topology. He also leaves open, in this page and the next, the existence of a smallest strict stratification refining or adapted to a given partition into tame locally closed pieces.
missed.quote: * comment énoncer que la top. de I est la top. quotient ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical stratifications in o-minimal geometry exist but are treated with other formalisms. A poset-map formulation of the minimal adapted stratification is a natural, partly open foundational question.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual facts (Alexandrov topology, the specialization adjunction) are classical. What is notable is that Grothendieck, in unpublished 1981-82 notes, formulates stratifications precisely as continuous maps to Alexandrov posets, decades before this became the standard definition in Lurie and in exodromy. He also has intrinsic fidelity and frontier criteria. This is a priority and context point rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'i.e. [-une partition-] une partition X = ∪ X_i^*' should read 'i.e. une pseudo-partition X = ∪_{i∈I} X_i^*' (pieces may be empty; the next page also uses 'pseudo-partition').
In 'Ord∘Esp = id_ℰ' and 'Esp∘Ord → id_𝒪' the subscripts are mathematically swapped. Mathematically these should be id_𝒪 and id_ℰ; check whether the slip is in the manuscript.
'base d'ouverts : les ens I_{≥x} = cl{x} (ou disons l'adh. pour I°)': this is the closure in the opposite preorder I°, not in I; the transcription is fine, but read accordingly.
'(NB "un générique" ... doivent être distingués !)' is uncertain. The sense is that distinct points should not have the same closure (generic points distinguished), i.e. T0.
The marginal note at top right ('* comment énoncer que la top. de I est la top. quotient ...') is largely illegible; it concerns the quotient topology of I and conditions on the X_i^*.
